newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Troubled Lithuanian state bank gets new capital.
newsitem.headline: Troubled Lithuanian state bank gets new capital.

text.p: Lithuania's third-largest bank, the state-owned State Commercial Bank, on Friday had some 165 million litas of new capital registered by the central bank, a key step on its road to recovery.
The bank was on the verge of insolvency after plunging into a liquidity crisis because of a portfolio of bad loans.
The government, mindful of a crisis in the bank sector only a few months ago, acted fast to rescue the troubled institution.
Most of the new capital, 155 million litas, consists of a special issue of government securities which will replace the bad loans on the bank's books.
A special bad loan agency has been created to get bad loans off the balance sheets of the State Commercial Bank and other banks, including commercial banks.
The banking system has made a recovery from the crisis but analysts say confidence is still fragile.
